# bank/

## Modules
- **Statement import**: `bankImportService.ts` (persist parsed rows, bulk upload w/ per-file account validation), `bankStatementParseService.ts` (pure format parser), `bankStatementOcrService.ts`, `bankStatementDedupHelpers.ts`.
- **Bank feeds / open banking**: `bankFeedService.ts`, `bankFeedConnectionService.ts`, `bankFeedOAuthService.ts`, `bankFeedSyncService.ts`; `openBankingService.ts` (facade — extension | manual_csv), `openBankingConnectionService.ts`, `openBankingSyncService.ts`, `openBankingTypes.ts`.
- **Reconciliation + allocation**: `bankReconciliationService.ts` (start/complete/autoMatch), `bankAllocationService.ts` (allocate/split/reverse, posts JE), `bankTransactionQueryService.ts`, `bankTransactionLookupService.ts` (resolve a tx by the statement reference, either column), `bankMatchCandidatesService.ts`, `bankMatchDbQueries.ts`, `bankTxLock.ts` (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` for every write path), `bankTxStatusMutations.ts` (match/unmatch/exclude), `bankTransferAutoLink.ts` (counterparty leg), `bankRuleAutoPostLine.ts` (one auto-post candidate).
- **Categorisation rules**: `bankRulesService.ts` (CRUD), `bankRulesMatchingService.ts` (`applyRules`, auto-create JE when `auto_create_entry=true`).
- **Multi-doc / 3-way match**: `multiDocMatchService.ts`, `multiDocMatchHelpers.ts` (pure).
- **VLM (AI extraction)**: `vlmService.ts` (facade), `vlmCore.ts` (vLLM HTTP client + health), `vlmInvoiceService.ts`, `vlmBankService.ts`, `vlmStatutoryService.ts`, `vlmSupplierStatementService.ts`, `vlmBankMatchService.ts`.
- **Receipt → JE**: `receiptToJournalService.ts` (pure).
- `index.ts` — barrel (conflict files excluded).

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/bank/*`. Every DB function takes `companyId` first. VLM services are stateless (no tenant storage); caller persists output under their `companyId`.

## Main function signatures
- `importBankStatement(companyId, bankAccountId, parsed) / importParsedTransactions(...)`.
- `startReconciliation(companyId, input) / completeReconciliation / createAdjustmentEntry(companyId, reconId, input)`.
- `lockBankTransactionForUpdate(companyId, txId)` (`bankTxLock`) — company-scoped `FOR UPDATE` read, `null` for missing/other-tenant; throws outside a request transaction; 5s `lock_timeout` → `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError`. Every write path calls it first.
- `allocateTransaction(companyId, txId, allocationInput, userId)` — posts JE; VAT account via `systemAccountResolver` (subtype) then fallback codes 1140/2120.
- `splitAllocateTransaction`.
- `reverseReconciledTransaction(companyId, bankTxId, userId, opts?: { postingAgent?, reversalDate? })` — unwinds the application, posts the contra, then resets the tx to `imported`. `opts.postingAgent` is forwarded to `reverseJournalEntry`; omit it and the contra stays `human:<userId>`. `opts.reversalDate` names the contra's date; omitted, it is the original entry's date when that period is open and today otherwise. **Refuses PRE-WRITE** when the period covering the resolved date is closed or locked (`Cannot reverse: the fiscal period covering <date> is not open …`) — `no_period` is NOT refused, because `createJournalEntry` auto-creates the fiscal year. All of its writes — unwind, contra and bank-line reset — share ONE savepoint, so a failure leaves invoice, payment, allocations and bank line untouched.
- `listAgentPostings(companyId, from, to, limit?)` (`agentActivityService`) — journals with `posting_agent LIKE 'mcp:%'`. Returns `reversed` (from `reversed_at`, NOT `status` — reversal never flips status) and `reversalOfId`.
- `importStatementForAgent(args)` / `undoImportBatch(companyId, batchId)` / `bankGlAccountBelongsToCompany(companyId, accountId)` (`bankStatementImportService`) — parse → hash-dedup → persist, for the MCP import tools. `undoImportBatch` returns `null` for another company's batch and deletes only `status='imported'` rows, reporting the allocated ones it refused.
- `findBankTransactionsByReferences(companyId, refs[], bankAccountId?)` / `findBankTransactionsByReference(companyId, ref, bankAccountId?)` (`bankTransactionLookupService`) — ONE query for the whole batch (a join against `unnest($refs)`, two arms — one per column), `Map` keyed by trimmed reference. EXACT match after trimming both sides (`btrim(x, E' \t\n\r\f')`, matching migration 519's expression indexes) against `reference` FIRST, falling back to `bank_reference` only when `reference` matched nothing. Oldest first, capped at 25 per reference; each candidate carries `matchedReference` + `matchedColumn`. Returns every candidate: the caller decides what more-than-one means (the MCP tools refuse it). Never LIKE — a prefix match resolves `INV-1` onto `INV-10`.
- `findBankTransactionAllocationStates(companyId, ids[])` (`bankTransactionLookupService`) — `{id, status, matchedJournalLineId}` for a whole set of ids in ONE query, keyed by id; an id absent from the map does not exist in this company. Reads BOTH columns on purpose: a row carrying `matched_journal_line_id` is already in the ledger whatever `status` says, and it is what `reverse_bank_allocation_batch` navigates by. `bulk_allocate_bank_transactions` calls it once for up to 500 resolved ids before it posts anything (the singular `getBankTransactionStatus` stays for the one-line tools).
- `applyRules(companyId, txId)` — rule evaluation by priority ASC (lowest = highest).
- `buildExpenseJournalFromReceipt(extracted, mapping)` — pure.
- `extractWithVlm(file) / extractBankStatementWithVlm / extractStatutoryDocWithVlm` — vLLM HTTP call, 120 s default timeout.

## Business rules
- **A bank account is a `gl_accounts` row with `account_subtype='bank'`.** `bank_transactions.bank_account_id` FKs to `gl_accounts(id)` — the column name misleads. Every row in dev and production honours this. The separate `bank_accounts` table is vestigial metadata (1 row dev, **0 rows production**): `bank_feed_connections.bank_account_id` still points at it, but nothing else may. Use `hasBankAccount` / `countBankAccounts` rather than counting `bank_accounts`; migration 446 dropped `bank_import_batches`' FK to it for the same reason.
- `bank_transactions.status`: `imported → matched → allocated → reconciled`.
- Allocation runs under `withTransaction`: JE post + transaction status update atomic.
- VAT account resolution: `account_subtype` first, then hard-coded codes 1140 (input) / 2120 (output) for pre-mig-327 companies — fallback must stay.
- Dedup is a CONTENT HASH of (date, amount, description, balance) — `bankTransactionHash.ts`. There is no reference in it and no `bank_reference` key: two genuinely separate same-day transactions with the same amount and description collapse into one (known limitation). Adding the reference to the hash is correct on a clean slate and a REGRESSION here, because every row imported before 2026-09-07 has a null reference and would no longer match its own statement on a re-import.
- **Known limitation — the 2026-08-27 `parseAmount` comma fix moves the dedup content hash.** A CSV row written SA-style ("1 234,56") used to parse as 123456 and hashes on the amount, so the same file re-imported after the fix hashes differently: the corrected row lands as a NEW transaction beside the wrong one rather than replacing it. Re-importing such a file is therefore a two-step job — delete the mis-parsed rows (or undo the batch) first, then re-import. Production carried no exposure as of 2026-08-27: there were zero CSV-sourced `bank_transactions`, and all 38 ABSA batches were PDFs, which go through `bankPdfParserUtils.parseAmount` and are untouched by this change.
- `autoMatch` is NOT atomic — each tx updated individually; mid-run crash leaves partial matches, next run picks up the rest.
- PRD-06 Phase 4: receipt → invoice auto-match links unallocated receipts to open AR invoices.
- Open-banking providers Basiq/Tink/Plaid are NOT implemented. They used to fall through to a random sample-transaction generator that INSERTed invented rows as `imported` and reported success (K-018). `createBankFeedConnection` now refuses them and `syncBankFeed` throws the exported `BankFeedProviderNotImplementedError` for a legacy connection rather than importing anything. Route callers must map that error to a 4xx — `withAuth` ROLLBACKs on >= 500 and would discard the `markSyncFailed` audit trail.
- VLM: `VLLM_BASE_URL`, `VLM_MODEL`, `VLLM_API_KEY`, `VLLM_TIMEOUT` env vars; `isVlmAvailable()` for health.

## Recent changes

- 2026-09-07 (same review, LOW): **the tool description over-promised the reference, and a header named a refusal mechanism nothing calls.** `import_bank_statement` claimed a Reference column is "read and stored" flatly — true for the generic and ABSA HEADER CSV layouts, FNB CSV, OFX, QIF and MT940, and false for `bankCsvParserStandard.ts` (standard_bank / capitec / nedbank — the token `reference` does not appear in that file at all), for the ABSA LEGACY positional layout (`reference: null` by construction), and for every PDF parser. An agent told the reference will resolve gets NOT_FOUND on those formats, which is precisely the class of defect this programme exists to remove. The description also gave the dedupe hash as (date, amount, description) when `bankTransactionHash.ts` includes `balance` as a fourth part. Both corrected. Separately, `allocationApplyRoute.ts`'s header asserted "every refusal must come from `invoiceSkipReason` BEFORE the first write" — `invoiceSkipReason` is exported and called by NOTHING, and was already dead before this branch. The header now names what actually refuses on each path (`partitionAllocationLines` for the batch, `signMismatchReason` plus the apply services' own pre-write validation for the single line). **The dead export is left in place, not removed:** wiring it up would turn a mid-write throw into a pre-write refusal on the single-line path, which is a behaviour change and someone's decision, not a comment correction.

- 2026-09-07 (adversarial review of the sign fix): **the UNATTENDED poster had the same defect, and fixing the Reference column made it more reachable.** `buildAutoCreateLines` (`bankRulesMatchingHelpers.ts`) received `isDeposit` and consumed it in the `account` arm ONLY — the supplier arm always emitted DR AP / CR Bank and the customer arm always DR Bank / CR AR, exactly as `allocateTransaction` did. `findMatchingTxs` filters on account, `status='imported'`, `matched_journal_line_id IS NULL` and an ILIKE; there is **no sign filter**, so any `auto_create_entry` rule matching a supplier's name matches that supplier's REFUNDS too and posts each as a payment, with no human in the loop. **Second order, and the part that makes it this change's problem rather than a neighbour's:** persisting the CSV Reference column activates `match_field IN ('reference','both')` rules, which previously matched nothing because every CSV-imported row carried a null reference. The P1 half of the change increased exposure to the P0 the first draft had not fixed. Both entity arms now flip on `isDeposit`, VAT included — a refund CREDITS `vat_input` rather than debiting it — and the default description no longer calls a refund `Payment to X`. The VAT KEY was already alloc-type-derived here (`bankRuleAutoPostLine.ts`), so only the direction was wrong. That path mints no payment document and runs no 4-way match, so it needed no other gate. Sweep of everything else the Reference column newly activates: `bank_reference` resolution (`bankTransactionLookupService`) is the intended target; `bankTransactionQueryService` search widens harmlessly; `bankMatchDbQueries` prefers `description` so it is unchanged; `vlmBankMatchService`'s 0.95-confidence reference heuristic would newly fire but **the module has no callers** (exported from the barrel only). `auto_create_entry = false` rules are suggestion-only (`bankRulesMatchingService.ts:84`), so the poster fixed here is the only one.
- 2026-09-07 (same review): **a pre-write guard that fronts a mid-write throw must use the throw's own thresholds.** `signMismatchReason` first passed a ZERO line through, justified by a comment claiming `skipReasonForInvoice` would refuse it. It does not — `skipReasonForInvoice(state, id, 0)` against R500 outstanding runs `0 > 500.01`, which is false, and calls the line POSTABLE. It then reached `validateBankSupplierPayment` (`tx.amount >= 0`) or `validateBankReceiptApplication` (`tx.amount <= 0`), which throw MID-WRITE — past the point `bulkAllocationSkip` can skip around it — so the registry savepoint unwinds every other line. One R0.00 statement line would have destroyed a 500-line batch, the single outcome that file exists to prevent. The guard now refuses zero outright. The lesson generalises: the comment asserted an invariant nobody had executed, and the test asserted the same false invariant beside it.

- 2026-09-07: **an allocation's DIRECTION follows the sign of the bank line, and a refund is not a settlement.** `allocateTransaction` computed `isSpent` and used it in two of its four branches. `supplier` always posted DR Accounts Payable / CR Bank and `customer` always posted DR Bank / CR Accounts Receivable, whatever the sign — so a supplier REFUND (money in) was booked as a payment out, crediting the bank the statement says was debited and leaving the account wrong by TWICE the line. Nothing failed: the call returned success, the row read as allocated, and the only symptom was a bank balance that no longer tied with no unallocated line to point at. **R261,651.64 on Velocity Fibre** across five lines (RohCap +R120,290 in FY26; four FY27 on-account refunds), found only by diffing the GL against the bank on (date, signed amount). The customer arm carried the mirror bug with no occurrence yet. Three things followed the sign and each was wrong on a refund: (1) `vatAccountKey` was direction-derived, so a supplier refund reached for vat_OUTPUT — a refund reverses the original purchase, so it reverses INPUT tax; the key now follows the alloc TYPE and only DR/CR follows the sign (the split path keeps the direction rule, having no entity). (2) The 4-way match flagged the most recent unpaid bill `payment_matched` for money coming back in — a settlement that never happened, on a bill the caller never named; gated on `isSpent`. (3) A customer refund minted a `customer_payments` row — a receipt for cash the company PAID, which lands in `list_unapplied_receipts` and on the statement as real cash; gated on `!isSpent`. **Every settler asks one rule, and the rule is in this module.** `signMismatchReason` (`bankLineDirection.ts`) — NOT in the MCP tool layer, because `pages/api/accounting/bank-match-confirm.ts` (the FindMatchModal's confirm endpoint) settles documents through arithmetic of its own and needed the identical answer. That route was the trap in this change: while `allocateTransaction` posted the payment direction unconditionally, a money-IN line matched to a bill posted DR AP / CR Bank AND reduced `amount_paid` — both wrong about the bank, both wrong the SAME way, so control and subledger stayed equal. Making the journal follow the sign broke that accidental symmetry and made the route WORSE: the journal now raises the AP liability while the route still reduces it, so AP control and AP subledger differ by TWICE the line behind a match a human confirmed on screen. Getting the GL right is not a licence to leave the subledger wrong. The route now refuses pre-write (`supplier_invoice`, `purchase_order` and `customer_invoice`; `bank_transfer` and `journal_line` settle no document and are deliberately absent), and PRE-write because `withAuth` decides COMMIT vs ROLLBACK on `statusCode >= 500` — a 400 raised after a write commits it. **The apply half is refused, not guessed.** `confirmReceiptMatch` / `applyBankLineToSupplierInvoices` take the ABSOLUTE value and apply it as a settlement, and there is no refund-allocation concept to route an inverted line to — so `signMismatchReason` (pure, in `allocationApplyRoute.ts`) refuses it PRE-write: a throw of `BankLineDirectionError` for the single-line tools, a SKIP with the same text in `partitionAllocationLines` for the batch, checked BEFORE the balance check so an impossible line cannot consume an invoice's remaining balance and push a correct line into "exceeds the outstanding".
- 2026-09-07: **the statement Reference column survives the import.** `mapCsvColumns` mapped date, description, amount and balance and nothing else, so a `Reference` column was read and discarded — `ParsedBankTransaction.reference` has always existed and `bankImportService` has always written it, only the header mapper never filled it in. The reference is the only stable key the CALLER controls and is what `bank_reference` resolves against in `allocate_bank_transaction` / `reverse_bank_allocation`, so losing it forced an importer to re-list every row and rebuild an old→new id map on (date, amount, description): **9,446 rows** of that on the Velocity Fibre rebuild. Matched EXACTLY against a list of reference header names, never by prefix — `reference` sits beside columns whose names contain it. A blank cell leaves the field UNSET rather than `''`, which would resolve nothing while reading as present. The dedupe hash is deliberately unchanged; see the Business rules note.

- 2026-09-03: **`bank_statement_coverage` decomposes the ledger-vs-statement gap into its two directions, and the decomposition is an EXACT identity.** `bank_transactions.amount` is signed and carries direction in the same convention as the GL bank leg — verified on all **9,097** matched rows across four production companies, where `bt.amount = jl.debit - jl.credit` to the cent with **zero** exceptions and no row in the opposite sign. So the matched halves cancel and `glBalance - computedBalance == glOnlyMovement - statementOnlyMovement`, checked against both audited companies at residual **0.00**. `fetchCoverageDirections` returns the two sides per account and `unexplainedResidual` reports what they fail to explain. It is non-zero in exactly one ordinary case, and that case is a finding: a recorded `bank_opening_balance` with **no journal behind it** sits in `computedBalance` and nowhere else, so the residual is minus that amount — the same defect `get_opening_balances` reports from the other direction. **Both directions matter and neither is visible from the other side.** Velocity has twelve 1610xxx paycard accounts carrying GL balances with ZERO bank transactions, mirrored by 1544xxx accounts carrying transactions that reached no journal; a report listing only "statement rows missing from the GL" finds half of it and reads as complete. **`getCashBalance` spans subtype `bank` AND `cash`** — nine production accounts are subtype `cash` (all seeded Petty Cash at R0.00, so no live figure moves), and petty cash is cash.

Production holds exactly one such completed reconciliation — R0.00 difference, zero matched transactions — and in every list and report it is indistinguishable from one that proved the whole account. Completion now requires a zero difference AND at least one matched transaction; failing either is a SUCCESS reporting `completed: false` with the reason, never a refusal, because by then `startReconciliation` and `autoMatchTransactions` have written and unwinding them would discard work the caller asked for.

- 2026-09-02: **cancel an in-progress reconciliation** (`bankReconciliationCancelService`, a separate file because `bankReconciliationService` is already over the 300-line cap). Starting a reconciliation claims every unmatched transaction on the account and there was no way out of one started on the wrong date or account. Cancel DELETEs the session and releases its rows: `matched` goes back to `imported` with `matched_journal_line_id` cleared, while `allocated`/`provisional`/`excluded` keep their status and their journal and are only detached — a matched row's link is reconciliation work, an allocated row's is a posted journal. - 2026-08-28: **the reference lookup labels a row once PER MATCHING REFERENCE, not once per row.** A transaction can carry one reference in `reference` and a DIFFERENT one in `bank_reference`, and a bulk call can ask for both. The first batched version decided each row's label from "did its `reference` match ANY reference in the batch?", so that row vanished from the second reference's candidates entirely: `['ZPC','ZPD']` resolved ZPD to nothing while a single lookup for ZPD found it — a silent NOT_FOUND that only appeared in batches. The query now JOINs `bank_transactions` against `unnest($refs)` in TWO arms (one per column, each a plain equality an expression index can serve) so the reference is part of the row's identity, and `ROW_NUMBER()` partitions by `(matched_reference, matched_column)`. `bankTxRefCandidateQuery(companyId, refs, bankAccountId)` is exported UNRUN so the DB-gated test can `EXPLAIN` the service's REAL statement (`.text`/`.values` off the lazy query) — the previous test planned a copy pasted into the test file, which stayed green when the service regressed to a bare `btrim()`. Known and accepted: with a large reference set the planner may hash-join the arms and scan the company once, which is still one scan for the batch rather than one per line.
- 2026-08-28: **reference resolution is BATCHED, PREFERENCE-ordered, and index-backed** (review follow-up to the entry below). `findBankTransactionsByReferences(companyId, refs[], bankAccountId?)` is now the real implementation — ONE query for a whole batch, returning a `Map` keyed by trimmed reference, with `ROW_NUMBER() … PARTITION BY matched_reference` capping candidates at 25 PER REFERENCE; the singular `findBankTransactionsByReference` is a thin wrapper. `bulkAllocationPrepare` resolved its selectors in a sequential per-line loop, so a 500-line bulk allocation issued 500 lookups inside a request that already holds every row's lock. **`reference` now WINS outright and `bank_reference` is consulted only for a reference that matched nothing in `reference`** — the two columns hold different KINDS of value (a printed reference vs a feed's opaque external id), so a cross-column collision is a coincidence, and a union let a feed id shadow the value the agent actually typed. `matchedColumn` rides along with `matchedReference` and the ambiguity reply names it, because "these three candidates came out of the feed's external id" is what a human needs to decide. Both branches are ONE SQL text (`$n::UUID IS NULL OR bank_account_id = $n::UUID`) rather than two copies that drift. **Trim set: `btrim(x, E' \t\n\r\f')`, not bare `btrim()`** — bare btrim strips SPACES ONLY, so an imported `"REF\r"` was unreachable from an agent that typed `"REF"` (JS `.trim()` strips it). No `\v`: PostgreSQL does not recognise it as an escape, so `E'\v'` is the letter `v` and would trim it off every reference. **Migration 519 adds `(company_id, btrim(reference, E' \t\n\r\f'))` and the same on `bank_reference`** — the expressions must stay character-for-character identical in the migration and the service or the planner silently reverts to a full company scan (isaflow_dev before: 9,132 rows removed by filter, 3,872 buffers, ~3.0 ms; after: BitmapOr over both indexes, 0 rows removed, 11 buffers, ~0.35 ms). A unit test reads the migration file and compares its expressions with the query's.
- 2026-08-28: **`findBankTransactionsByReference` matches EITHER `reference` OR `bank_reference`** — `WHERE company_id = $1 AND (btrim(reference) = $ref OR btrim(bank_reference) = $ref)`, both branches, still exact-after-trim, still capped at 25, and it now returns `matchedReference` (the stored value that matched) so a caller listing candidates can show which value each row carried. **`bank_reference` is vestigial-but-kept, and the statement reference lives in `reference`**: production on 2026-08-28 had 9,824 rows with `reference` and ZERO with `bank_reference`. Every statement path writes `reference` only — `bankImportService` (both inserts, so the MCP `import_bank_statement` route too), `bankStatementOcrService`, `bank-transactions-import-classified`, `bank-transactions-manual`, `sageMigrationCommitService`. The only writers of `bank_reference` are `bankFeedSyncService` and `openBankingSyncService`, and they store the PROVIDER'S EXTERNAL ID (`tx.id` / `tx.externalId`), not the printed reference — which is also why the fallback order is `bank_reference` first: where it exists it is the stabler handle. Do NOT drop the column: `allocateTransaction`'s `customer_payments` insert reads `tx.reference || tx.bank_reference || tx.description`, `bankTxRowMapper` maps it to `BankTransaction.bankReference`, and the feed dedup key is that column. Note the knock-on for the "dedup primary key is `bank_reference`" rule below: for file/OCR/manual imports that key is never populated, so those imports have always been running on the amount+date+description fallback.
- 2026-08-28: **a raced or locked row never aborts a bulk run.** `autoMatchTransactions` catches `BankTransactionAllocatedError` per iteration (`skippedRaced` in the result) and `applyRules` catches `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` per candidate (`autoPostSkippedLocked`) — both continue, anything else rethrows. This is not cosmetic: `withAuth` COMMITs on any handler that RETURNS, so an escaping error meant the route 400'd while the matches already applied were committed and the rest were silently skipped. `autoMatchTransactions` also sorts its matches by transaction id, same lock-ordering rule as the bulk tools. Every counter reaches the UI (`applyToast` + the rules page banner; autoMatch shows a notice on the reconciliation page) — a skip nobody can see reads as "rules aren't working".
- 2026-08-28: **`findMatchingTxs` caps a rule at `MAX_RULE_CANDIDATES` (500)** and fetches one row past it, so `applyRules` can report `autoPostTruncatedRules` ("re-run to continue"). Each candidate holds a row lock to the end of the request; unbounded, one rule over a large import locks the whole account for the run.
- 2026-08-28: **the counterparty auto-link runs in a SAVEPOINT** (`bankTransferAutoLink.ts`) instead of filtering error codes. EVERY pg error aborts its transaction, not just 40P01/40001/25P02 — the whitelist that preceded this could only cover the codes someone thought to list, and any other failure left the request aborted with every later statement raising 25P02 while the handler returned a journal id that could never commit. Rolling back to the savepoint discards the failed link and leaves the posted journal intact.
- 2026-08-28: **every bank-transaction write path takes a row lock on its first read** (`bankTxLock.lockBankTransactionForUpdate` — company-scoped `SELECT * … FOR UPDATE`). LOCKED: `allocateTransaction`, `splitAllocateTransaction`, `reverseReconciledTransaction` (bankAllocationService), `matchTransaction`, `unmatchTransaction`, `excludeTransaction` (now in `bankTxStatusMutations.ts`, re-exported from `bankTransactionQueryService`), and each candidate row in `bankRulesMatchingService.applyRules`' auto-post loop. NOT LOCKED, deliberately: every read-only query path (`getBankTransactions`, the lookup and match-candidate services), the post-UPDATE re-read at the end of an allocation (the row is already locked), `deleteTransactions` (its `status = 'imported'` predicate is the guard), and `bulkAcceptTransactions` — see the separate note below. Each of these read `status`, refused on the wrong one, then posted or rewrote the row; unlocked, two concurrent REQUESTS both passed the check and both acted — one transaction with two journals, or a status write landing on top of a freshly committed allocation and orphaning its journal. Since PR #264 every request is one transaction on the ALS client, so the lock is held for the rest of the request. The helper THROWS outside a request transaction (`FOR UPDATE` in an implicit single-statement transaction locks nothing), and `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` on the request client turns a wedged peer into `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` ("retry in a moment") rather than a pinned connection. That `SET LOCAL` is re-issued on EVERY call, never memoised: it is subtransaction-aware, so `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` restores the previous value — which is `0`, no timeout at all — and every MCP tool call and `withTransaction` runs in a savepoint that rolls back on failure. Caching it would remove the timeout exactly where contention is likeliest. The DB-gated test asserts more than the lock error: without the lock the second session still fails 55P03, because it blocks on the status UPDATE — *after* posting its second journal.
- 2026-08-28: **match/unmatch/exclude refuse a row that carries a posted journal** (`BankTransactionAllocatedError`, `status = 'allocated' AND matched_journal_line_id IS NOT NULL`; the bank routes' catch renders it as a 400). **`reconciled` is deliberately NOT in that guard** — a row only reaches it via `matchTransaction` (reconciliation promotes rows already `matched`), so its journal was written elsewhere and pre-dates the link; unmatching orphans nothing, and `BankTxTable` still offers Undo on those rows, so refusing would 400 a live button. Undoing an allocation is `reverseReconciledTransaction`'s job — it posts the contra. A row that is `allocated` with a NULL `matched_journal_line_id` is half-finished, not posted, so it is still allowed through: refusing would strand it. **`bulkAcceptTransactions` is the deliberate exception** — it is the bulk "accept as matched" action and its `status IN ('imported','allocated')` predicate means it knowingly moves allocated rows; it takes no lock and no journal check, so it can still relabel a row whose journal is posted. Left as-is because that is what the UI action means; if that ever changes, it needs the same guard.
- 2026-08-28: **the MCP bulk allocate and batch-reverse loops sort by transaction id before posting**, and `applyRules` locks its candidates in id order. Row locks are held to the end of the request, so two overlapping batches walking their rows in opposite orders deadlock (40P01); a total lock order turns that into one batch waiting for the other.
- 2026-08-28: **`allocateTransaction`'s counterparty auto-link catch rethrows 40P01 / 40001 / 25P02.** The auto-link is a nicety and an absent counterparty is genuinely non-fatal, but those three kill the whole request transaction — swallowed, the rest of the function issues statements that all raise 25P02 and the handler returns a journal id for a journal that can never commit.
- 2026-08-28: `bankTransactionLookupService.getBankTransactionStatus(companyId, txId)` — returns the row's status, or `null` for a missing row or another tenant's. Exists so the MCP allocate/reverse tools can answer their pre-write refusals from a READ: both services write BEFORE they can fail (`allocateTransaction` posts the entry then updates the row; `reverseReconciledTransaction` posts the contra then resets the row), so a `catch → toolError` around them cannot tell a refusal from a half-done write — and since a refusal frees the idempotency key, the retry writes a second time.
- 2026-08-28: `getAllocationBatchLines` LEFT-joins `bank_transactions` and returns `transactionExists`. An INNER join dropped a line whose transaction had since been deleted, so the batch silently reported fewer lines than it posted — the vanished one being exactly what a human needs to see.
- 2026-08-27: **`allocateTransaction`, `splitAllocateTransaction` and `reverseReconciledTransaction` CLEAR `bank_transactions.allocation_batch_id`.** The stamp says the row belongs to a bulk batch; that stops being true the moment the row is reversed or re-allocated, and nothing cleared it. Left set, `reverse_bank_allocation_batch` would walk the stamp and reverse whatever journal is on the row NOW — unwinding a posting the batch never made. `bank_allocation_batch_lines` (mig 515) is the second line of defence: it records the journal each line posted, so the reverse tool compares rather than trusting the column.
- 2026-08-27: statement import parser fixes. QIF — a `!Type:Bank` header shares the first `^` block with transaction #1, and filtering blocks that start with `!` silently dropped that transaction from every headed export; header LINES are stripped now, not whole blocks. ABSA — moved to `utils/bankCsvParserAbsa.ts` and mapped by header name: the current `Account Number,Transaction Date,Description,Amount,Balance` layout was undetectable (only the legacy Description1/Description2 one was), so the import was rejected outright. `detectBankFormat` now scans the first few lines for the header (exports carry a title row) and `parseAmount` reads SA-style "1 234,56" as 1234.56 rather than 123456. All of this reaches `import_bank_statement` unchanged — the MCP tool already routes through `parseStatement`.
- 2026-08-27: PRD-11 §4 — `bankAllocationBatchService` (`createAllocationBatch` / `recordAllocationBatchLines` / `getAllocationBatchLines` / `clearAllocationBatch`) backs the MCP bulk allocate + batch reverse tools. Mig 514 adds `bank_allocation_batches` and `bank_transactions.allocation_batch_id`. The stamp is on the TRANSACTION, not the journal: reversal starts from the transaction and must CLEAR the stamp so the row can be re-allocated into a later batch, which a posted-journal column could not allow. `recordAllocationBatchLines` throws unless every id was stamped — a posted journal outside the reversible set is exactly the failure the batch id exists to prevent — and `getAllocationBatchLines` returns `null` for another tenant's batch so the caller renders the generic NOT_FOUND.
- 2026-08-27: `contactDirectoryService` gained `suppliersBelongToCompany` / `customersBelongToCompany` (id array, one query, empty set skipped). The singular helpers would have been 500 round trips before the first journal of a full bulk allocation.
- 2026-08-27: PRD-11 §5 — `allocateTransaction` / `splitAllocateTransaction` build the journal date with `fmtDate` (`@/lib/neon`), not `toISOString()`. pg returns `transaction_date` at LOCAL midnight, so UTC rendering dated a 00:30 SAST transaction to the previous day — wrong month at a period boundary. The same date feeds the `customer_payments.payment_date` INSERT. `bankTransactionQueryService.fmtDate` (used by `mapTxRow`) still carries the same defect and was left out of scope.
- 2026-08-27: `bankTransactionLookupService` added so the MCP allocate/reverse tools can take the statement's `bank_reference` instead of a UUID.
- 2026-08-27: PRD-11 §3 — `getBankTransactions` returns `{ transactions, total, nextCursor? }`
  and accepts an opaque keyset `cursor` (base64url `{d,a,id}`). The keyset predicate
  (`bankTxCursor.ts`) must stay in lockstep with the ORDER BY, which now ends
  `, bt.id DESC` in every branch to make the ordering total; a malformed cursor throws
  `InvalidCursorError` before any query runs — as does a cursor whose date is not a real
  calendar date or whose id is not a UUID (both would otherwise reach a SQL cast), and a
  cursor combined with a non-zero `offset` (they compose into silently short pages). The row query fetches `limit + 1` and trims
  the probe row; `total` and the COUNT query stay unpaged. `offset` is unchanged and still
  what the UI route uses. Split out of the 300-line service: `bankTxRowMapper.ts`
  (`fmtDate`/`mapTxRow`, re-exported from the service), `bankTxQueryFragments.ts`
  (`TX_SELECT`, `allocationCond`), `bankTxFilters.ts` (`BankTxFilters`). The mapper's
  local UTC-rendering `fmtDate` is gone — it delegates to the one in `@/lib/neon`, so a
  00:30 SAST timestamp no longer lists (or cursor-pages) as the previous day.
- 2026-08-14: `hasBankAccountService` gained `countBankAccounts`; `/api/accounting/setup-guide` now uses it instead of counting `bank_accounts` rows, which meant the `bank-account` setup task could never complete in production.
- 2026-08-09: `bankStatementImportService` — shared parse/dedup/persist path for agent imports. `importParsedTransactions` gained `skipAutoPost`; the MCP path sets it so an import posts nothing (sweep attributes to the system user, which would escape `list_agent_postings`).
